c.v: The
HMAC
module uses SHA-256 as hash algorithm.
If the input message is not a multiple of 512 bits, a SHA-256 padding algorithm must be applied in software.
The SHA-256 padding algorithm is the same as described in Section
Padding the Message
of
FIPS PUB 180-4
As shown in Figure 21.3-1, suppose the length of the unpadded message is m bits.
Padding steps are as follows:
Append one bit of value "1" to the end of the unpadded message;
Append k bits of value "0", where k is the smallest non-negative number which satisfies m + 1 + k ≡ 448 (mod 512);
Append a
64-bit
integer value as a binary block.
This block includes the length of the unpadded message as a big-endian binary integer value m.
In downstream mode, there is no need to input any message or apply padding.
In upstream mode, if the length of the unpadded message is a multiple of 512 bits, the user can choose to configure hardware to apply the SHA padding.
If the length is not a multiple of 512 bits, the user must apply the SHA padding manually.
